I am 65 years old and have been farming this land in Quzhou for 40 years. I never went to school, but I know my fields the way you know your own face in the mirror. My farm is 13.1 mu — not big, but it is all I have. It is just me and my wife at home now. Our children work in the city and send a little money back when they can, but I do not count on that for farming. I have to make do with what I have.

This year, like every year, I will plant wheat in autumn and maize in summer on the same land. It is the only system I know, and it is what everyone in the village does. 

For the wheat, I will rotary till the field before planting in early October. I will buy improved wheat seed — the kind they call 502 at the shop, the same kind my neighbors use. I always put down two bags of urea per mu before planting. That is what I did last year and the year before, and it has worked. I will irrigate three times: once before winter so the wheat can survive the cold, once in spring when it greens up, and once when the grain is filling. Pumping water costs electricity, so I do not waste it, but three times is what the wheat needs. I will spray for weeds once, for bugs twice, and if I see any disease I will spray once for that too. I expect about 1000 jin per mu if the weather treats us kindly.

For the maize, there is no time to plow after wheat harvest — the window is too tight, maybe less than a week. I plant hybrid maize seed, denghai 605, right into the wheat stubble without tilling. I will put down a little bit of fertilizer, maybe a small handful per mu at planting, but not much — the wheat already took most of the nutrients out, and fertilizer bags are expensive. I will irrigate twice, at the jointing stage and when it is silking. I will spray twice for corn borers and once for weeds. No-tillage saves me diesel and time. I hope for about 1100 jin per mu.

I do not use phosphorus or potassium. Those colored bags cost too much, and I have never seen my neighbors get much better yield from them. My well gives me water when I need it, but I watch every yuan I spend on pumping. This is my plan. It is not fancy, but it has kept food on my table for 40 years.
